headline: KSE-100 crashed 3,078.56pts (-1.79%) to close at 168,865.04 as the US-Iran war escalated further (tanker/warship strikes over the weekend, Brent >$101/bbl) — market breadth was ugly (406 decliners vs 58 gainers of 464 traded). This pushes the drawdown from the Jan 23 ATH (189,556) to ~10.9% — PAST the 10% dry-powder trigger for the first time since tracking began. Individual holdings fell harder than the index (mostly -2% to -5.6%, broad panic selling, no company-specific news behind any single mover — MUGHAL was the day's weakest at -5.6% on no identifiable news, just high-beta cyclical amplification). Portfolio value ~Rs 10.02M, P/L ~-Rs 234,500 (~-2.29% on cost), down from yesterday's ~Rs 10.222M/-0.34% — a real one-day hit but exactly the kind of volatility a 10-25yr horizon is built to absorb. ACTION TAKEN: per the standing plan, redeploying roughly half of the AICF/MICF cash reserve (~Rs 250K of ~Rs 508K) into MZNPETF/MIIETF as a first tranche, keeping the rest in reserve in case the war pushes the correction toward 15%. AVN's EXIT call remains unexecuted (13 reviews now, no new news). Note prices reflect the ~13:39 PKT data snapshot (last available before today's extended Friday session); the KSE-100 close figure is confirmed against multiple news sources.
market: KSE-100 closed Fri Sep 11 at 168,865.04, down 3,078.56pts (-1.79%) from Thursday's 171,943.60 — the sharpest single-day drop in this run of red sessions, as the US-Iran war entered a new phase: the US and Iran traded strikes on oil tankers and warships over the weekend/this week, Iran-backed Houthis hit Saudi Arabia, and Brent crude is holding above $101/bbl on fears of a prolonged Strait of Hormuz disruption. Market breadth was extremely weak (406 decliners vs 58 advancers), a sharper ratio than Thursday's already-broad 293-vs-162. DRAWDOWN TRIGGER CROSSED: from the Jan 23, 2026 ATH of 189,556, today's close puts the drawdown at ~10.9% — the first close past the 10% line that the standing plan earmarked for shifting AICF/MICF dry powder into MZNPETF/MIIETF. Given the war is still live and unresolved (started Feb 28, 2026, now escalating rather than cooling), a full one-shot deployment felt like catching a falling knife — redeployed roughly half now, kept the rest in reserve in case this deepens toward the 15% mark, at which point the standing guidance calls for a heavier shift. SBP's next MPC meeting is Sep 14, 2026 (3 days away) — surveys still point to a hold at 11.5% as the base case (84-87.5% expect no change) despite CPI running ~10.18% average in the first two months of FY27, though the odds of a small hike aren't zero given the currency/import-cost pressure from $100+ oil. DRAP drug-pricing review: unchanged since early September — pharma associations still opposing the pricing-formula changes, nothing enacted. AVN — no new company news since the Aug 28 H1/Q2 FY26 loss filing; EXIT call unexecuted through 13 reviews now, stock down another 3.3% today to Rs 27.80 (-38.3% on cost). EFERT — no new news; Q3 results not yet due. DATA QUALITY: stock prices are the ~08:39 UTC (13:39 PKT) snapshot — the last one available before today's extended Friday session (2:32-4:30pm PKT) that the automated fetch cron doesn't fully cover — so today's real closing prices per-stock may be somewhat worse than shown here, consistent with the confirmed index-level close being lower than the snapshot would suggest. Fund NAVs (funds_updated: Aug 13) are now 29 days stale — the MUFAP scraper issue remains unresolved and is a GitHub-Actions-side network/WAF problem, not something fixable from this local session; ~28% of portfolio value is still priced off a month-old NAV snapshot. GIT/DEPLOY: local git still cannot reach github.com over the standard git protocol (third consecutive review with this issue) — commits from the Sep 9 and Sep 10 reviews remain unpushed alongside this one; raw.githubusercontent.com and api.github.com both work fine, so this looks like a routing/firewall issue specific to github.com's main frontend, not a broader outage. Push will be retried; if this keeps recurring, worth checking the local network/proxy/DNS config for github.com specifically.

entries.basis: Monthly-timeframe accumulation zones for a 10-25yr horizon: where fundamentals + monthly support align to add in small portions. 'entry' = start nibbling at/below; 'add' = deeper monthly support to load more. Pakistan macro-aware (SBP 11.5%, KSE-100 off the Jan ATH). These are accumulation guides, not precise buy/sell signals — verify with your broker.

MZNPETF.note: Broad Islamic index ETF — your #1 DCA vehicle. Accumulate on any dip; entry is just under fair value, add = deeper monthly support.

MIIETF.note: Second index-ETF leg. Same DCA logic — buy small and often, more at the add level.

MEBL.note: Core compounder but ran up (~556). Start adding on a pullback to ~540; back up the truck at/below Rs 500 (the standing allocation line).

MIF.note: Actively managed Islamic equity fund (NAV-based). Accumulate on monthly dips.

BWCL.note: Cement upcycle, dividend payer, FY26 profit +7.1% but on softer operating margins. Accumulate near monthly support ~460, more at 435.

GLAXO.note: Defensive pharma with pricing-deregulation tailwind. Add on dips to ~322.

DCR.note: REIT — income play with steady rental dividends. Add for yield near ~38; inflation hedge.

EFERT.note: INCOME, not growth (WATCH). Only add for the yield near ~174; urea glut keeps upside capped — don't overweight.

AIRLINK.note: HIGH BETA, policy-dependent — cap the position. Only small adds near ~125; trim on sharp rallies.

FFL.note: Turnaround, KEEP SMALL. Tiny adds only near ~14.5; take profits if it runs 50%+.

AVN.note: NOT a buy. H1 FY26 swung to a net loss (EPS -0.62); the thesis is broken. This is an exit candidate, not an accumulation — do not average down.

UPFL.note: Only 3 shares (~Rs 77K), illiquid. Exceptional company but immaterial to portfolio decisions — no accumulation plan.
